summary: The first half of the week brought a selloff, a beat and a mixed picture. Stocks fell Monday and Tuesday, with the S&P 500 sliding about 1% Tuesday to a five month low as tech, chips and software led and all 11 sectors finished lower. October retail sales rose 0.2%, a touch above forecasts, while industrial production fell 0.4% on a utilities drop and the Empire State survey sank to 7.8. Chair Warsh spoke about AI and productivity but gave no rate signal, so a December hike stays priced. Nvidia then beat with $115.8B in revenue and guided to $130B, sending Nasdaq futures up almost 1% Wednesday morning. Target and Lowe's beat, though both traded lower early. Still ahead: the FOMC minutes at 2:00 PM today, Palo Alto tonight, jobless claims, the Philly Fed, Walmart and the Anthropic IPO debut Thursday, and Intuit after Thursday's close.

headline.title: Thursday Nov 19: Walmart, jobless claims and the Anthropic IPO debut
headline.body: After Nvidia's beat steadied the AI trade, Thursday tests the consumer and the IPO market. Walmart reports before the open with consensus EPS of 0.64, jobless claims and the Philly Fed land at 8:30 AM ET, and Anthropic is expected to begin trading after pricing Wednesday evening. Intuit, Ross and Gap report after the close. The FOMC minutes Wednesday at 2:00 PM set the rate tone going in.

spotlight.name: Nvidia
spotlight.when: Tue Nov 17, after the close, call 5:00 PM ET
spotlight.watch: Reported: revenue of $115.8B beat the roughly $109.1B consensus and EPS of 2.68 beat 2.47. Q4 guidance of $130B topped $125.1B, plus a $150B buyback. Shares spiked then faded after hours, and were up near 3% premarket Wednesday.

spotlight.name: Walmart
spotlight.when: Thu Nov 19, before the open, call 8:00 AM ET
spotlight.watch: Whether Walmart raises full year guidance, and what it says about lower and middle income shoppers heading into the holidays.

spotlight.name: Home Depot
spotlight.when: Tue Nov 17, before the open, call 9:00 AM ET
spotlight.watch: Reported: EPS of 3.86 versus 3.87 expected on revenue of $43.4B, and CFO Richard McPhail was named CEO effective Nov 23. Shares fell about 2.5% Tuesday.

macro.name: Empire State manufacturing survey (Nov)
macro.note: Fell to 7.8 from 25.5, well below the roughly 17 to 18 expected, as new orders dropped to 3.0. Employment improved to 18.1.
macro.react: A sharp miss that pointed to cooling factory demand, though it was quickly overshadowed by the tech selloff and the Nvidia buildup.

macro.name: Fed Chair Warsh, opening remarks at Fed productivity and jobs conference
macro.note: Warsh called this a hinge point for the economy and focused on AI, productivity and jobs, warning of possible disruption. He did not comment on the near term rate outlook.
macro.react: No new signal on December, so the hike stayed priced. Stocks sold off Monday and Tuesday on tech and chip worries rather than on his remarks.

macro.name: China industrial production and retail sales (Oct)
macro.note: Monthly activity data for China. Exact release day was not confirmed by previews.
macro.react: Weak retail sales would revive stimulus hopes and could lift China linked names, while a broad miss would weigh on copper and miners. Impact on US indexes is usually modest.

macro.name: Retail sales (Oct)
macro.note: Rose 0.2% versus about 0.1% expected, with September revised to 0.8%. Excluding autos and gas, sales rose 0.5%.
macro.react: A modest beat that did little to change the hike story. Stocks fell anyway, with the S&P 500 down about 1% to a five month low and the Dow down about 1.6% as tech and software led the slide.

macro.name: Import and export prices (Oct)
macro.note: Prices of goods coming into and leaving the US, a pipeline signal for goods inflation. Result not confirmed by public recaps.
macro.react: A hot import price reading would add to inflation worries already in place after CPI. Usually overshadowed by retail sales at the same time.

macro.name: Industrial production and capacity utilization (Oct)
macro.note: Fell 0.4% versus a 0.1% gain expected, the biggest drop since January, as utilities output plunged 4.3%. Manufacturing rose 0.3% and utilization slipped to 76.4%.
macro.react: The miss was utilities driven while factory output was solid, so markets largely looked past it.

macro.name: NAHB homebuilder index (Nov) and business inventories (Sep)
macro.note: NAHB fell four points to 25 versus 29 expected, its lowest reading since April 2012.
macro.react: Added pressure on homebuilders on a day when all 11 sectors finished lower.

macro.name: Fed speaker: Waller
macro.note: Governor Waller speaks on payments, though questions on policy are likely.
macro.react: Hawkish comments that lean toward a larger December move or more hikes in 2027 would lift the 2 year yield and the dollar and weigh on long duration tech. Signs of patience after the softer PPI would trim the roughly 10% odds of a half point hike and help growth stocks. A quarter point hike in December is already close to fully priced.

macro.name: Housing starts and building permits (Oct)
macro.note: Early reports put starts at a stronger than expected 1.31 million annual rate, while building permits came in weaker than expected.
macro.react: Strong starts but soft permits send a mixed signal for builders. Markets focused on Nvidia, with Nasdaq futures up almost 1% before the open.

macro.name: Pending home sales (Oct)
macro.note: Contract signings on existing homes, a lead on closings. Previews expect a significant decline.
macro.react: A large drop is largely expected and would mainly weigh on housing stocks and mortgage lenders.

macro.name: 20 year Treasury bond auction ($13B)
macro.note: A test of demand for long dated debt with yields near multi year highs.
macro.react: A weak auction with a large tail would push long yields higher and pressure stocks into the minutes. Strong demand would ease that pressure.

macro.name: FOMC minutes (Oct 27 to 28 meeting)
macro.note: Details of the meeting where the Fed held rates with two dissents for a hike. Watch how many officials saw a hike as likely soon and any debate on a larger move. Released today at 2:00 PM ET, with the 10 year yield near 5.1%.
macro.react: Minutes showing broad support for hiking, or talk of more than one hike, would lift short yields and the dollar and hit tech. A divided or cautious tone would ease fears of a half point move and help growth stocks. A December hike is already priced, so the path beyond it matters most.

macro.name: UK CPI (Oct)
macro.note: UK inflation after the Bank of England's recent hike.
macro.react: A hot print would support more Bank of England tightening, lift gilt yields and the pound and can spill into Treasuries. A soft one would ease global yield pressure.

macro.name: Bank Indonesia rate decision
macro.note: Another emerging market central bank leaning toward tightening.
macro.react: Mostly a local market event. A surprise hold would weigh on the rupiah.

macro.name: Initial jobless claims (week of Nov 14)
macro.note: Weekly layoffs data. Claims remain very low, consistent with a tight labor market.
macro.react: A drop toward 190,000 would add to hike conviction and lift yields. A jump above 215,000 would be an early crack in the labor story and would rally bonds and rate sensitive stocks.

macro.name: Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey (Nov)
macro.note: Factory conditions in the mid Atlantic region, including a prices paid gauge.
macro.react: A strong reading with rising prices paid would add to inflation worries and lift yields. A sharp drop would help bonds. Watch the prices components.

macro.name: Leading economic index (Oct)
macro.note: The Conference Board's composite of forward looking indicators.
macro.react: Rarely moves markets.

macro.name: Kansas City Fed manufacturing survey (Nov)
macro.note: Another regional factory read.
macro.react: Minor market impact.

macro.name: Fed speaker: Vice Chair Jefferson
macro.note: Vice Chair Jefferson speaks on economic shocks, a chance to hear leadership views after the minutes.
macro.react: Hawkish comments that lean toward a larger December move or more hikes in 2027 would lift the 2 year yield and the dollar and weigh on long duration tech. Signs of patience after the softer PPI would trim the roughly 10% odds of a half point hike and help growth stocks. A quarter point hike in December is already close to fully priced.

macro.name: University of Michigan consumer sentiment, final (Nov)
macro.note: Final November read on consumer mood, plus 1 year and 5 year inflation expectations.
macro.react: Rising inflation expectations would lift yields and support the hawkish case into the weekend. A drop in expectations would help bonds and tech. Sentiment itself is near historic lows and moves markets less than the inflation gauges.

macro.name: Fed speaker: Governor Cook
macro.note: A final Fed voice for the week.
macro.react: Hawkish comments that lean toward a larger December move or more hikes in 2027 would lift the 2 year yield and the dollar and weigh on long duration tech. Signs of patience after the softer PPI would trim the roughly 10% odds of a half point hike and help growth stocks. A quarter point hike in December is already close to fully priced.

macro.name: Global: Japan CPI (Oct), UK retail sales (Oct), Lagarde speech
macro.note: A cluster of global releases. Exact days were not confirmed by all previews.
macro.react: A firm Japan CPI could support Bank of Japan tightening and firm the yen. Impact on US indexes is usually small.

notes: Earnings shows large market cap names and widely traded movers, not every report. EPS figures are consensus estimates from Robinhood data and can differ from other sources; reported figures are Robinhood actuals. Spotlight ranges combine Robinhood with public previews. Names without a confirmed timing or estimate, such as XPeng and Futu, are left out.

Consensus figures come from public week ahead previews and can change. Where sources differ, a range is shown. Some global release days were not confirmed and are listed as Times vary. Revenue figures are from public previews.
Reaction notes are scenario thinking, not predictions.
